correctness.rationale: A connected nonempty subset must occupy consecutive columns; a column is internally connected and the only adjacent occupied states without a rail connection are opposite singletons. For a fixed interval, the unsigned ending-state count p_m,p_m,q_m starts at (1,1,1) and q_{m+1}=2p_m+q_m stays odd. Thus the parity of the total C_n is the parity of the triangular number n(n+1)/2. All unnormalized Walsh multipliers have that same parity, proving nonvanishing in residues 1 and 2. For signed extension the new singleton sums are alpha(1+t+d), beta(1+b+d) and the new double sum is alpha beta(1+t+b+d); the constant terms start a new interval and their signed totals update z. Starting from zero, the three seed pairs give (1,-1,-1,-1), (1,-1,0,-1), (2,0,-1,0). On the repeated block the next states are (2,0,-2,0), (1,1,-1,1), (-1,1,-2,-1), (2,0,-1,0), closing the cycle. This exhibits zeros in residues 3 and 0 and absolute magnitude 1 in residues 1 and 2, including n=1,2 from the seed. Zero frequency attains C_n, the triangle-inequality upper bound. The Walsh basis is orthogonal, so the condition number in invertible cases is the ratio C_n/1. An independent bit-frontier connectivity enumeration and integer transform for all characters through n=8 reproduces C_n and the zero counts 0,0,9,66,0,0,870,7462, the attained minimum in invertible orders, and each stated certificate value.
residual_risks: Replay is finite and is not used for the all-size conclusion. The magnitude-one claim concerns the invertible orders only; no full singular-spectrum classification is made.

value.rationale: The connected-vertex-set family is classical, but its signed indicator convolution has a meaningful information-loss and conditioning question absent from ordinary counts. An explicit lost character at every singular size and a character attaining the sharp norm of inversion at every invertible size are substantive exact results, not just the parity observation.
